domain: Political Philosophy / Migration Studies / International Law
topic_summary: Analysis of immigration as a contested kernel where the border commitment is read through sovereignty-primary or freedom-of-movement-primary lenses. Each reading instantiates structurally different constraints with distinct victim sets: sovereignty readings place excluded migrants in the victim set, while freedom-of-movement readings place displaced citizens or welfare recipients in the victim set.

key_entities: Nation-state (territorial authority claiming monopoly on legitimate border enforcement)
Prospective migrants (individuals seeking entry across borders)
Current citizens (residents with legal status in destination state)
International human rights regime (normative framework claiming universal personhood rights)
Labor markets (economic mechanism mediating wage/employment effects)
Welfare systems (redistributive mechanisms funded by taxation)
key_tensions: State sovereignty vs universal human rights (territorial control vs freedom of movement as human right)
Citizen preference vs migrant welfare (democratic mandate to restrict vs humanitarian obligation to admit)
key_mechanisms: Border enforcement apparatus (visa systems, deportation, detention)
Labor market competition (wage suppression or complementarity depending on skill distribution)
Fiscal redistribution (tax-funded services accessed by new entrants)
key_absences: Colonial/imperial history creating migration pressures (why certain populations seek entry)
Capital mobility asymmetry (capital crosses borders freely while labor faces restrictions)

readings.expected_structural_delta: Refugee/non-refugee distinction creates bifurcated victim set; moderate ε on categorical exclusion

omegas.description: Capital crosses borders freely while labor faces restrictions. Is this asymmetry a Mountain (economic efficiency) or a Snare (extraction favoring capital over labor)? Sovereignty reading treats it as legitimate; freedom-of-movement reading treats it as extractive.

Labor market effects vary by skill level (high-skill complementarity vs low-skill substitution). Does this bifurcate the victim set within each reading, or does it collapse the readings into one constraint with skill-conditional victims?
omegas.source: Independence Testing (Type B overlap between labor_market_competition and readings)

omegas.description: Border enforcement is selectively applied (visa overstays vs border crossings; high-skill vs low-skill). Does selective enforcement reveal sovereignty reading as Snare (extractive class sorting) rather than Rope (legitimate coordination)?

Refugee Convention definition (persecution) excludes climate/economic displacement. As climate migration increases, does humanitarian_obligation_reading collapse into sovereignty_reading (no obligation) or expand toward freedom_of_movement_reading (general admission)?

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel decomposition successful: three readings instantiate genuinely different constraints with distinct victim sets. Sovereignty reading places excluded migrants in victim set; freedom-of-movement reading places displaced citizens in victim set; humanitarian reading creates categorical bifurcation. Deferred axes (labor_market_competition, fiscal_redistribution_strain) are empirical mountains/ropes feeding into readings, not readings themselves.
